subject: net
title: Subnetting
procedure: Splitting IPv4 networks into subnets (CIDR, VLSM)
promptTemplate: Give an IPv4 network and requirements for the subnets. easy: subnets of equal size. medium: VLSM with 3 subnets. exam: VLSM with 4–5 subnets and transfer networks. Asked for: network address, prefix, broadcast, first/last host per subnet. When checking: each row on its own, check for overlaps and order (largest first).
answerFormat: Table: subnet | network address/prefix | first host | last host | broadcast.

drills.prompt: What is the network address of `192.168.10.77/26`?
drills.explanation: /26 means blocks of 64 addresses: 0, 64, 128, 192. 77 lies in the block starting at 64.

drills.prompt: What is the broadcast address of `192.168.10.77/26`?
drills.explanation: The block 64–127: the last address is the broadcast.

drills.prompt: How many usable host addresses does a /27 subnet have?
drills.explanation: 2^(32−27) = 32 addresses, minus network and broadcast address.

drills.prompt: What is the longest prefix length (smallest subnet) that still fits 50 hosts?
drills.explanation: A /26 has 64 − 2 = 62 usable addresses; a /27 only 30.

drills.prompt: Write the subnet mask of a /21 in dotted decimal notation.
